summary: The checked ground-state coercivity and conservative rescaling algebra support their uses. The noise probability argument requires divergence of the imaginary component; arbitrary growth of complex modulus does not give its claimed auxiliary limit. The final theorem is not refuted.

problems.title: The nonconservative component, not merely complex modulus, must diverge in the probability step

source_locator.page_convention: one-based PDF pages equal printed pages

problems.claim_paraphrase: The theorem uses phi -> infinity for a spatially constant complex coefficient with nonzero imaginary part; the proof claims that the fixed-threshold probability for the fourth power of the L4 norm of h tends to zero.
assumptions: X0(x)=exp(-|x|^2) is deterministic H1(R3); its squared H1 norm is 4*(pi/2)^(3/2)
phi_1^(1)=n+i is spatially constant with Im=1 nonzero
the special noise assumptions of Theorem 1.7 replace conservative hypothesis (H)
C3 is finite, positive, deterministic and depends only on fixed T and initial-data norms

independent_check.kind: analytic proof with exact symbolic identity verification
independent_check.formula: hat_mu=b^2-i*a*b; h=exp(-2*b*B_t-2*b^2*t); integral h^4 dt has law b^(-2) I, I=integral_0^infty exp(-8*B_s-8*s)ds
independent_check.counterexample: phi_n=n+i: |phi_n| -> infinity while h and the probability in (8.44) are identical for every n.
independent_check.positive_tail_proof: For any finite q, choose K with exp(8K-16)>q. The positive-probability event B1 in [-K-2,-K-1] and sup_{0<=s<=1}|B_(1+s)-B1|<1 implies I>q.

problems.result: The auxiliary limit (8.44) is false under unrestricted |phi| -> infinity. The limit is proved under |Im phi| -> infinity. This does not prove the final non-blow-up theorem false.
counterevidence: Fixed-direction amplification phi=lambda*phi0, lambda real positive and Im phi0!=0, is a plausible intended convention and makes the argument valid.
The reduced PDE and spatially constant phase show existence does not depend on Re phi at fixed Im phi, but this does not determine whether its probability is already one.
No journal-final text equivalence or author-confirmed intended limit was established.
problems.core_dependency: Step 3 supplies high probability that both nonlinear contraction stopping times reach T in Theorem 1.7. Conservative Theorems 1.2 and 1.5 are unaffected.
problems.severity_reason: An admissible narrower reading remains unresolved; it is not graded Major by assuming an interpretation the authors may not intend.

correction.statement: State |Im phi_1^(1)| -> infinity, or explicitly scale a fixed nonconservative complex direction.
correction.verified_scope: Brownian scaling and the fixed-threshold probability limit only, conditional on the preceding deterministic estimates.

resolved_candidates.location: p.12, stochastic sum over basis index j and Brownian mode k
resolved_candidates.status: aggregate bound independently reconstructed; no PDE counterexample promoted
resolved_candidates.detail: The diagonal intermediate display is not a valid general scalar BDG inequality when the same Brownian driver occurs for different j. Keeping sum_j inside the square then applying Cauchy-Schwarz yields the final bound actually needed. This supports the intended interchange without claiming each displayed intermediate inequality is valid.
X0=0 gives X=0 and a linear stochastic wave. Finite-horizon boundedness suffices for no finite-time blow-up; a uniform bound on an infinite interval is not asserted by this review.

problem_checks.source_locations: Theorem1.7 p6; equations2.12-2.16 p10; proof constants and equations8.40-8.45 pp36-37.
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: Writing phi=a+ib gives Re(hat_mu)=b^2 and h=exp(-2*b*B_t-2*b^2*t). With s=b^2*t and Brownian scaling, its fourth-power integral has law b^(-2)*I. Finite positive I follows from Brownian sublinear growth and continuity. For phi_n=n+i the entire h path law is unchanged, and the positive Brownian tube event in the report indeed forces I>q for every finite q. The displayed unrestricted auxiliary probability limit therefore fails along this family; amplifying a fixed nonreal direction yields |b| to infinity and restores this exact step.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: The source explicitly treats the constant complex-noise model separately from conservative hypothesis(H). It does not explicitly define the direction of phi to infinity. The report correctly retains the natural fixed-direction reading and does not infer blow-up or falsity of the theorem from failure of a sufficient bound. Journal VoR correspondence remains unverified.
problem_checks.severity_check: Needs Evidence correctly reflects the unresolved intended limit convention; no unconditional Major asserted.
problem_checks.other_report_check: The aggregate BDG reconstruction keeps basis sums inside the square; the displayed source diagonal step on p12 does not justify a general independent-driver estimate. The report preserves its bounded algebraic correction without claiming a PDE counterexample.
